description:
The back-edge reduction check is the minimum sequence.

Today (machine.md M13; src/compiler2/native_codegen/terminator.rs:703-730), every back edge runs:
`mov x0,x21; ldr w1,[x0,#0x458]; sub; str; cmp; mov x25,x2; b.le`
That is 7 instructions. The `mov x0,x21` copy of the process register and the `mov x25,x2` copy are dead on the common (no-yield) path.

Fix: load, decrement and branch on the process field directly. Move any copies the yield path needs into the yield path. Coordinate with fz-sc8.249, whose hypothesis is that the inlined yield slow path drives callee-saved register traffic. A cold out-of-line yield stub may serve both.

Asm first: target listing for the back edge (`ldr w1,[x21,#0x458]; subs w1,w1,#1; str w1,[x21,#0x458]; b.le yield`, or better if the counter can live in a register across the loop).

Acceptance: p00 falls by the counted instructions (bench). Yield behaviour is unchanged: the scheduler fixtures and fz-wje's reduction-parity test pass.
title: The back-edge reduction check is the minimum sequence
